delete_after.description:
What became of the delete the request asked for with `delete_after`; absent when it did not
ask. Whatever it says, `outcome`, `counts` and `held` are the move's alone.

restore_point.description: What became of the restore point.

timings.description: The broker's timing marks (M3_DESIGN.md §9.1): for measurement only; a client ignores it.

DeleteAfter.description:
The second step of `plan.execute {delete_after}`: what became of the items the run had just moved
into quarantine. Anything not counted in `purged` is still in quarantine and can be put back.

kept.description: Quarantined items of the run that were offered and are still in quarantine.

DeleteAfterOutcome.description: How the delete step of `plan.execute {delete_after}` ended.

oneOf.description: Every quarantined item of the run was approved and deleted.
Some were deleted; the rest (declined, or not deletable now) are in quarantine.
The "Delete now" dialog was cancelled or could not be shown: nothing was deleted.

The run left nothing in quarantine that can be deleted now (nothing was moved, or the session
is held: not recorded completely, items waiting for a restart or a retry).

The step failed before or while deleting (the store was busy or refused); what was not
deleted is in quarantine.

HeldItem.description: An item left in place because it is locked.

Locker.description: A process that holds a file open, as Restart Manager reports it.

service.description: Short name of the service, when the process is one.

OpId.description:
The number of one op within a session, counted from 1 in plan order.

Every selected plan item gets an op id, whether or not it ends up acted on. The id also names the op's
directory and backup files, through [`OpId::file_stem`]. Reading `0` fails: no op has that id. That
an id is at most the header's item count is checked where the journal is read.

Outcome.description: What a run did. Carried by results; not an error.

oneOf.description: Everything was done.
Some items are held or failed; the result names them and what holds them.
An undo restored what it could and lists conflicts.
The session was not recorded completely; History offers recovery. Wins over the two above.

OutcomeCounts.description: How many items ended in each [`ItemOutcome`]. Every field reads as 0 when missing.

RestorePointOutcome.description: What became of the restore point (§7.7). Serialised as an object tagged by `"kind"`.

oneOf.description: The policy did not ask for one.
A restore point was created.
Windows skipped it because another one was created within the last 24 hours.
System Restore is turned off.
Creating it failed. The run went on: restore points supplement quarantine, never replace it.

SessionId.description: UTC start time and 64 random bits, e.g. 20261115T101502Z-9f3a6c1d2b7e4a50

ms.description: Milliseconds since the broker process was created, on a monotonic clock.

wall_unix_ms.description: The wall clock at the mark, milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

TimingName.description: A step of the elevated flow the broker times.

oneOf.description: `main` passed the DLL-search and working-directory restriction (process mark).
The client passed the pipe checks and its `engine.hello` was answered (process mark).
`uninstall.prepare` began.
`uninstall.prepare` harvested every program, stored each fingerprint and opened the sessions.
`leftovers.scan` began.
The first `*.progress` line of the request was written to the pipe.
`leftovers.scan` built its scan and counted the bands.
`plan.create` bound and froze the plan.
The consent dialog was up and could be answered.
The consent dialog ended (any answer).
`plan.execute` handed the approved plan to the executor.
The executor returned its run.

Timings.description: The `timings` member of a result: for measurement only (M3_DESIGN.md §9.1); a client ignores it.

marks.description: The process marks, then the marks of this request, in the order they were taken.

process_created_unix_ms.description:
When the broker process was created (`GetProcessTimes`), milliseconds since the Unix epoch;
absent when it could not be read (the marks then count from the broker's own start).
